extract: Tumor tissue and  normal adjacent (juxta) tissue  samples were obtained from early stage, untreated patients with NSCLC. Tumor tissue samples were obtained from surgical specimens, after macroscopical examination of the tissue by a pathologist. Tissue samples were stored in C02-independent medium (Invitrogen) with 5% human serum and transferred within 1-hour post-surgery to the research institute. For each specimen, a fragment was formalin-fixed, and paraffin embedded for histology and immunohistochemistry. Tumor tissue samples were gently cut in approximately 1mm3 pieces. Tissues were digested enzymatically, by an incubation of 20-40 minutes, based on the size of the tissue, at 37oC in agitation, in C02-independent medium (Invitrogen) with Collagenase I (2mg/ml, Sigma-Aldrich), Hyaluronidase (2mg/ml, Sigma-Aldrich) and DNase (25Âµg/ml, Sigma-Aldrich). Tissue fragments were gently triturated with a 20 ml syringe plunger on a 40 Âµm cell strainer (BD) in 1X PBS (Invitrogen) with 1% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 2mM EDTA (Gibco), until uniform cell suspensions were obtained. The suspended cells were subsequently centrifuged for 10 minutes at 400g.  Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were isolated using Ficoll-Paque PLUS solution (Sigma-Aldrich). After tissue digestion, cells are resuspended in C02-independent medium and layered onto Ficoll-Paque PLUS solution. Subsequently cells were centrifuged for 20 minutes at room temperature at 800g without breaks. After centrifugation tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were carefully transferred to a new tube and washed with 1X PBS with 1% FBS and 2mM EDTA (Gibco). CD3+ T cells were isolated using the Pan T cell Isolation Kit (Miltenyi), that leads to approximately 80% purity.  CD3+ T cells were resuspended 1X PBS with 1% FBS and 2mM EDTA (Gibco). Cell numbers and viability were measured using a Countess II Automated Cell Counter (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and hemocytometer/ trypan blue.   For isolation of the distinct CD8+ T cell subsets, upon TILs isolation, cells were washed and resuspended in 100ul staining buffer containing antibodies. After 20 minutes incubation at 4oC, cells were washed twice and resuspended in 200ul of 1X Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) buffer with 1mM EDTA and 1% fetal bovine serum. Cell sorting was performed using MoFlo ASTRIOS cell sorter from Beckman Coulter Life Sciences. Cells were stained with a combination of surface markers, using a set of monoclonal antibodies from the following:  CD3-AF532 (1:50, clone UCHT1, #2067979, Thermofischer Scientific), CD8-BV510 (1:50, clone 2ST8SH7, #9259590, BD Biosciences), PD1-BV421 (1:40, clone EH12.2H7, #B268454, Biolegend), KLRG1-PE-Cy7 (1:40, clone SA231A2 ,#B256810, Biolegend), TIM3-BV786 (1:40, clone 7D3, #9259393, BD Biosciences), CD39-APC (1:50, clone eBioA1, 2#2071264, Thermofischer Scientific). Cells were gated on single cells based on the FSC-A/FSC-H and SSC-A/ SSC-H scatters, live cells (Zombie NIR negative), CD3+, CD8+ cells and afterwards on the population of interest, on the basis of the expression of the protein markers: KLRG1, CD103, PD1, TIM3 and CD39.   Upon sorting of the CD8+ subsets, cells were centrifuged at 300g for 3 minutes, resuspended in 350ul of TCL buffer (QIAGEN) with 1% b-mercaptoethanol inside a 1.5ml eppendorf tube and rapidly stored at -80oC. Within a period of a maximum 7 days, cells were thawed and prepared for RNA isolation. Norgen single cell RNA purification kit was used for RNA extraction. Residual genomic DNA was removed using the RNase free DNase set (Qiagen). RNA quantity and quality was measured by Agilent RNA 6000 Pico kit (Agilent Technologies). Samples with high quality RNA (RIN>7) were further selected. On average the samples had between 500pg-1ng of total RNA. To synthesize and amplify cDNA from those samples, the SMART-Seq v4 Ultra Low Input RNA kit (TaKaRa) was used, according to manufacturerâs instructions. cDNA quantity and quality were measured by High Sensitivity DNA kit (Agilent Technologies). 9ng of amplified cDNA was used for library synthesis, using the KAPA HyperPlus library preparation kit (Roche) according to manufacturerâs instructions. Sequencing libraries were quantified with the LabChipÂ® GX Touchâ¢ nucleic acid analyzer and libraries were sequenced on a HiSeq4000 sequencer (Illumina). extract: Cells were "superloaded" at 150,000 cells per 10X Chromium controller lane, on 20 lanes (for a total of 3 million cells), and scRNA-seq and dialout libraries prepared as described below.,1) scRNA-seq libraries were prepared using 3â scRNA-seq V3 kits (10X Genomics), according to manufacturer instructions. Note that the 10x Indexes were a mix of 4 oligos for each library (each starting with a different base to avoid sequencing biases). Thus each scRNAseq library has 4 fastq files (denoted _a, b, c & d).,2) From the initial amplified cDNA, we used a two stage PCR protocol to generate âdialoutâ libraries, for each lane. Because the CROP-seq vector expresses a PolII polyadenylated transcript that ends just downstream of the guide sequence, the dialout libraries identify the sgRNA sequences associated with each droplet. In several cases multiple libraries were made for a sample. Libraries without ".2" in their name (e.g. Dialout_2kg_11AMDox_4_ATTACTCG) were sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq machine. Others, e.g. "Dialout_2kg_11AMDox_6.2_CGCTCATT" were sequenced on an Illumina Novaseq machine, together with scRNA-seq libraries.
processing: Fastq files were de-multiplexed by index primer,Demultiplexed fastq files for the same sample, with the same index, and from the same sequencing run were concatenated,1) Note, for each scRNAseq library, there were four 10xGenomics index primers for each library, designated SAMPLEID_a _b _c & _d.,1) All scRNAseq libraries, except "scRNAseq_2kG_2PMDox1_6", were sequenced on a 2nd NovaSeq run, and fastq files from those runs are designated "_NS2_",1) Fastq files were uploaded to the 10X genomics server to run CellRanger (which maps reads to the human genome, assigns reads to the distinct CellBarcodes (CBCs) for each droplet, and counts reads in each droplet for all transcripts in the human genome.,1) CellRanger distinguishes droplets with true cells from droplets with debris or ambient RNA, and generates a matrix of genes by CBCs (the filtered feature barcode matrix), which was used for downstream analysis.,2) Dialout libraries linking CBCs to guides were sequenced to saturation (~40x coverage) using either Illumina NextSeq (files w/o ".2") or Novaseq (files with ".2" in the name).,2) Dialout read 1 covers the 10x Genomics barcode/CBC and UMI. Read 2 covers 24 invariant bases of U6 promoter sequence before reading into the guide protospacer sequence,For the Supplementary file: _Dialout_guides_per_CBC.txt, 1) dialout reads with fewer than 4 exact duplicate were removed to reduce noise from PCR chimeras, 2) for each cell barcode x guide combination, the number of distinct Unique Molecular Identifiers (UMIs) was counted. The guide with the highest number of UMIs, plus 2nd, 3rd and 4th place guides were recorded.,For the Supplementary file: _aggregated.2kG.library.mtx.gene_x_cell.RDS.gz. Matrix files for each sample were merged, and assigned column names:Â  TARGETGENE:GUIDESEQUENCE:CBC-SAMPLNAME & rows as SYMBOL:ENSEMBLID, and then subset to only those CBCs called as singlets (in the calls.csv files for each sample, and also, across all samples, in _Dialout_guides_per_CBC.txt).,For the Supplementary files: _ALL_{log2fcs,Pvalues}_dup4_s4n3.99x.txt, we applied edgeR to the RDS genes x singlets table (with sample ID/10X lane number as a covariate), to detect differentially expressed genes for singlet cells with guides to each target (up to 15 guides) versus singlet cells with non-targeting or safe targeting guides. Individual edgeR results tables for each contrast were then aggregated to give genes x perturbation tables of log2 fold changes & p.values, respectively.,For the remaining supplemental files: To identify sets of genes that are co-expressed across single cells in a dataset, we applied consensus non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) (Kotliar, D. et al. Identifying gene expression programs of cell-type identity and cellular activity with single-cell RNA-Seq. Elife 8, (2019).) to the Genes x Singlet cells counts matrix. NMF decomposes an input cell x gene read count matrix (X) into (i) a cell x components matrix (W) and (ii) a component x gene matrix (H), such that X = W â¢ H. The cell x component matrix W represents the contribution of each component to the cellâs transcriptional profile, and the component x gene matrix H encodes information about gene expression programs, e.g. housekeeping and cell cycle pathways. Consensus NMF performs this analysis 100 times, to identify components that are stable regardless of starting conditions. Based on several metrics, we chose 60 for the number of components (K).,Supplementary file: 2kG.library.usages.k_60.dt_0_2.consensus.txt, is the consensus Cell x Components matrix, from cNMF.,Supplementary file: 2kG.library.spectra.k_60.dt_0_2.consensus.txt, is the consensus Components x Genes matrix, from cNMF.,Supplementary file: 2kG.library.gene_spectra_score.k_60.dt_0_2.txt, is a variant of the Components x Genes matrix that identifies genes that are most representative of each component as those that have a high specificity z-score (zero if that gene has the same weight across all components, and high if that gene is weighted strongly only for one component). We refer to genes with high specificity scores for a component as a "program".,Supplementary file: 2kG.library_MAST_DEtopics.txt, is a Perturbation x Program matrix measuring the association of cells with guides to a given target with specific programs, using Model-based Analysis of Single Cell Transcriptomics Package (MAST, Finak, G. et al. MAST: a flexible statistical framework for assessing transcriptional changes and characterizing heterogeneity in single-cell RNA sequencing data. Genome Biol. 16, 278 (2015)). to compare the expression of each program in cells carrying gRNAs targeting a given gene vs cells carrying control gRNAs (safe-targeting and negative control guides), including 10X lane as a covariate to account for batch effects. Values are MAST scores.,Supplementary fil: Table.S2.X.AllMASTStatisticalTestResults.txt, is a second table of MAST outputs for Perturbation effects on programs, including log2 fold changes (of Program gene expression with each perturbation), p. values and FDRs (either across all 60 programs, or across all 60x2357perturbations (experiment wide FDR)). Program IDs are given as K for the analysis (always 60) underscore Program # (e.g. 60_15 is Program 15).,Assembly: hg19,Supplementary files format and content: Matrix files (.mtx). Filtered feature barcode matrices with rows=genes and columns=cell barcodes, and values=read counts, for all high quality cells called by CellRanger. Includes all reads from each sample (both Novaseq runs). To read, in R, do: library(Matrix);mymatrix=readMM("filename"),Supplementary files format and content: Barcodes files (barcodes.tsv). The list of cell barcodes (CBCs) for high quality cells. Use for column names of the extracted matrix file.,Supplementary files format and content: Features files (features.tsv). Tab delimited table of gene names (symbols & ENSEMBL gene numbers) quantified by CellRanger. User for row names of the extracted matrix file. Features should be the same for all sample matrices.,Supplementary files format and content: Singlet calls files (calls.tsv). Tab delimited table, with header row, with columns: CBC_10x (cell barcode, in the same order as barcodes.tsv), Guide (guide protospacer sequence), Genec(gene/target of top guide), UMI_count (# of UMIs for guide with most UMIs), Good_singlet (1 if cell is a singlet, as defined by having >=4 UMIs for the top guide and <=4x fewer than this for the next most frequent guide), Multiplet (1 if singlet, 2, 3 or 4 for doublet, triplet or quadruplet, 0 if no guide was assigned to the cell (e.g. 3 or fewer UMIs for the top guide, including entries for CBCs w/ no guides detected).,_Dialout_guides_per_CBC.txt, is tab delimited text recording dialout guide reads for each CellRanger-called cell CBC. Reads that were duplicated less than 4 times were removed from the analysis, to reduce the influence of PCR chimeras generated in Dialout library construction, after which counts of distinct UMIs associated with each guide detected for each CBC were made. Column IDs: gene_symbol=Target ID/gene symbol for top guide, X10x_cbc (10x Barcode for droplets called as containing cells, with an extension indicating lane: 1 to 6 for 11AMDox samples 1 to 6, 7 to 13 for 2PMDox1 samples 1 to 7, and 14 to 20 for 2PMDox2 samples 1 to 7),  guides_per_cbc= number of guide reads detected for that CBC, umis_per_cbc=total distinct UMIs in guide reads per CBC, max_umi_ct=the number of distinct UMIs for the guide with the most UMIs, guide_w_max=sequence of that guide, X2nd_place_umi_ct, X3rd_place, X4th_place= UMI counts for guides with the 2nd, 3rd or 4th most UMIs. CBCs with 4 or more UMIs for the top guide and less than or equal to 1/4 of this for the next most frequent guide were considered to be singlets (1 cell & 1 guide/droplet) for further analysis.,_aggregated.2kG.library.mtx.gene_x_cell.RDS.gz. RDS format genes x cell matrix (genes=rows, CBCs=columns) for all cells called as singlets (>=4 UMIs for top guide & <=1/4 this for 2nd to top guide). Column names are formatted as Â  TARGETGENE:GUIDESEQUENCE:CBC-SAMPLNAME & rows as SYMBOL:ENSEMBLID. To access, gunzip, then, in R, do: readRDS("_aggregated.2kG.library.mtx.gene_x_cell.RDS"),_ALL_log2fcs_dup4_s4n3.99x.txt (tab delimited). Differential expression log2 fold changes for all cells with guides to a given target versus all cells with non-targeting or safe targeting guides (by edgeR, using lane number as a covariate),_ALL_Pvalues_dup4_s4n3.99x.txt (tab delimited). Differential expression raw p.values for all cells with guides to a given target versus all cells with non-targeting or safe targeting guides (by edgeR, using lane number as a covariate),2kG.library.usages.k_60.dt_0_2.consensus.txt, is the consensus Cell x Components matrix, from consensus non-negative matrix factorization (cNMF, see data processing steps, below)..,2kG.library.spectra.k_60.dt_0_2.consensus.txt, is the consensus Components x Genes matrix, from cNMF.,2kG.library.gene_spectra_score.k_60.dt_0_2.txt, is a variant of the Components x Genes matrix that identifies genes that are most representative of each component as those that have a high specificity z-score (zero if that gene has the same weight across all components, and high if that gene is weighted strongly only for one component). We refer to the set of genes with high specificity scores for a component as a "program".,2kG.library_MAST_DEtopics.txt, is a Program x Perturbation matrix measuring the association of cells with a given perturbation (guides to a given target) with specific programs, using Model-based Analysis of Single Cell Transcriptomics Package (MAST, Finak, G. et al. MAST: a flexible statistical framework for assessing transcriptional changes and characterizing heterogeneity in single-cell RNA sequencing data. Genome Biol. 16, 278 (2015)). MAST was used to compare the expression of each program in cells carrying gRNAs targeting a given gene vs cells carrying control gRNAs (# safe-targeting and negative control guides), including 10X lane as a covariate to account for batch effects. Values are MAST scores.,Table.S2.X.AllMASTStatisticalTestResults.txt, is a second table of MAST outputs for Perturbation effects on programs, including log2 fold changes (of Program gene expression with each perturbation), p. values and FDRs (either across all 60 programs, or across all 60x2357 perturbations (experiment wide FDR)). Program IDs are given as K for the analysis (always 60) underscore Program # (e.g. 60_15 is Program 15).

processing: Custom programs were used to demultiplex individual samples using their unique index. We used CLC Genomics Workbench 7 for RNAseq alignment and statistical analysis of the data. Human HG19 was used as reference sequence.,To calculate gene expression intensity, read counts were normalized to reads. Methods for data normalization and analysis are based on the use of âinternal standardsâ (Rocke DM, Durbin B. A model for measurement error for gene expression arrays. source: Mesenchymal stem cells isolated from hiPSCs derived brain organoid named hiPSC-nMSCs
extract: Strand-specific RNA-seq (ssRNA-seq) libraries were prepared according the manufacturer's instructions using the Illumina Standard RNA sample library preparation kit (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA).,After quantification using the Agilent 2100 bioanalyzer (Agilent, Santa Clara, CA, USA), the strand-specific libraries were sequenced on an Illumina HiSeq X ten instrument that generatedpaired-end reads of 150 nucleotides.
processing: Illumina Casava1.7 software used for basecalling.,Sequenced reads were trimmed for adaptor sequence, and masked for low-complexity or low-quality sequence, then mapped to mm8 whole genome using bowtie v0.12.2 with parameters -q -p 4 -e 100 -y -a -m 10 --best --strata,Reads Per Kilobase of exon per Megabase of library size (RPKM) were calculated using a protocol from Chepelev et al., Nucleic Acids Research, 2009. In short, exons from all isoforms of a gene were merged to create one meta-transcript. The number of reads falling in the exons of this meta-transcript were counted and normalized by the size of the meta-transcript and by the size of the library.,Supplementary files format and content: tab-delimited text files include RPKM values for each Sample ...

extract: Total RNA was extracted from ECs using RNeasy Plus Mini Kit (Qiagen),RNA-Seq libraries for mRNA profiling were prepared from 1.5-5  Âµg total RNA using the NEBNextÂ® UltraTM RNA Library Prep Kit for IlluminaÂ® (NEB, USA) following manufacturerâs recommendations
processing: Library preparations were sequenced on an Illumina Hiseq4000 platform and 150 bp paired-end reads were generated,Reference genome and gene model annotation files were downloaded from genome website browser (NCBI/UCSC/Ensembl) directly. Indices of the reference genome were built using Bowtie (v2.2.3) and paired-end clean reads were aligned to the reference genome using TopHat (v2.0.12).,HTSeq (v0.6.1) was used to count the read numbers mapped of each gene, followed by calculation of RPKM (Reads Per Kilobase of exon model per Million mapped reads) of each gene based on the length of the gene and reads count mapped to that gene,Differentially expressed genes were then determined using DESeq R package (v1.12.0). The resulting P-values were adjusted using the Benjamini and Hochbergâs approach for controlling the False Discovery Rate (FDR). Genes with an adjusted P-value<0.05 and FDR<0.005 were assigned as differentially expressed.,Genome_build: hg19; mm10,Supplementary_files_format_and_content: tab-delimited text files include RPKM values for each Sample ...

extract: Using ICELL8 multisample nanodispenser (Wafergen Biosystems), 50nl (3E4/ml) of the live cell or nuclear suspension was precisely dispensed into an ICELL8 nanowell microchip containing 5184 wells (150nl capacity) as described previously (Goldstein et al., 2017). Assuming a Poisson distribution frequency for the number of cells per well, about 30% of the nanowells were expected to contain a single nucleus under optimal conditions. Automated scanning fluorescent microscopy (using Olympus BX43 fluorescent microscope with a robotic stage) of the microchip was used to select ~1400 wells containing a single live cell or a single nucleus (CellSelect software, Wafergen Biosystems).  The candidate wells were manually evaluated for debris or clumps as an additional QC.,The chip was subjected to freeze-thaw in order to lyse the cells and 50 nl of reverse transcription and amplification solution (following ICELL8 protocol) was dispensed using the multisample nanodispenser to candidate wells. SCRB-seq was then performed on the candidate wells using pre-printed primer that adds a well-specific barcode to the (A)n mRNA tail of the cellular transcript. The cDNA libraries were pooled, concentrated (Zymo Clean and Concentrator kit, Zymogen) and purified (using 0.6x AMPure XP beads). 3â transcriptome enriched library was made by Nextera XT Kit and 3â-specific P5 primer, and sequenced on Illumina Hiseq2500.
processing: Illumina Casava software used for basecalling. Individual FASTQ files obtained were demultiplexed using the well-specific barcode identifiers for downstream data processing and analysis.,FASTQ sequences were mapped to human genome hg19 (GRCh37) downloaded from UCSC genome browser website and aligned using TopHat2,Transcript structure and abundance were estimated using HTseq and Cufflelink,Read count profile were analyzed for the differential expression analysis using DESeq2 (version 1.10.1),Genome_build: hg19,Supplementary_files_format_and_content: tab-delimited text files include read count values for each Sample ...
